question: Point out the FALSE statement regarding sarcoidosis:

options.opa: The presence of parenchymal infiltrates without hilar involvement in pulmonary sarcoidosis indicates a stage III.
options.opb: The most sensitive method to detect interstitial lung disease in sarcoidosis is the measurement of CO diffusion capacity (DLCO).
options.opc: An increase in the number of total lymphocytes in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) as well as a CD4 / CD8 ratio of less than 3.5 in broncalveolar lavage is highly suggestive of sarcoidosis.
options.opd: The elevation of the angiotensin conversion enzyme in blood above 2 times its normal value is congruent with the diagnosis of sarcoidosis, although its sensitivity and specificity are low.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Parenchymal infiltrates without hilar involvement" -> "Stage III pulmonary sarcoidosis" -> "Correct classification" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Measurement of CO diffusion capacity (DLCO)" -> "Detection of interstitial lung disease" -> "Most sensitive method" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Increase in total lymphocytes in BAL" -> "CD4/CD8 ratio less than 3.5" -> "Highly suggestive of sarcoidosis" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Elevation of angiotensin conversion enzyme in blood" -> "Above 2 times normal value" -> "Congruent with sarcoidosis diagnosis" -> "Low sensitivity and specificity" -> 80%
analysis: Option opc is the false statement. In sarcoidosis, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) typically shows an increase in the CD4/CD8 ratio, often greater than 3.5, due to the accumulation of CD4+ T-helper cells. A CD4/CD8 ratio of less than 3.5 is not highly suggestive of sarcoidosis and is more indicative of other interstitial lung diseases.
